chapter: Early bands around Bay St. Louis
title: Early bands: Paul Maurice, Oscar Collins and the faking band
summary: Harry lists the players in the early Bay St. Louis bands led by Paul Maurice, with Collins on trombone, and notes they faked rather than read.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: All right. Oscar Collins, Paul Maurice, Johnny Tonequale, Eddie Thomas, Ogie Socia, and, um... What about Eddie Thomas the drummer? Yeah, Eddie Thomas the drummer and Giger, Anderson Edward, the bass player. Well, what was Ogie's playing at that time? Oh, I got, I got, I got that messed up too. Because Oscar Collins was the trombone playing, both of them couldn't be in the same band. Later, I played with Ogie. Oscar Collins was the trombone playing this band, you see. And Maurice? And Maurice. What did he play? Clarinet. Who was the leader?
I don't even get that. Collins was the leader? No, Paul Maurice was the leader.
And, uh, this Johnny, I can't pronounce his name, I can't get that name. Johnny was in there? Johnny Tonequale. Tonequale.
T-O-M-T-R-A-Y. And what did he play? Trumpet. Tonequale.
Tonequale. Tonequale. Was that a faking band or a reading band?
Oh yeah, that's a faking band. You started out fake?
